description: Somos un equipo de estudiantes de Mecatrónica de la UTEQ con experiencia en electrónica, programación, control y sistemas embebidos. Participamos en el hackathon de la UNAQ para crear un sistema de monitoreo de salud para astronautas y llevarlo hasta un prototipo funcional.
summary: HEALTHYX is a health monitoring system for astronauts that applies Total Productive Maintenance principles to the human body. ESP32 nodes send vital signs over HTTP to an onboard system that uses I-MR control charts and linear regression to detect and predict anomalies in real time. A cyclic memory keeps recent data onboard, while the full history is sent to Earth for precise clinical analysis.
details:
HEALTHYX is a health monitoring system for astronauts, developed by team EXPANYX, a group of Mechatronics Engineering students from UTEQ. Our approach comes from our field: we treat the human body as a complex machine and apply Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) principles to predict, prevent, and correct anomalies in vital signs before they become a problem.

How it works:

  1. Data collection: ESP32 microcontrollers act as sensor nodes and send vital signs (heart rate, blood pressure, SpO₂, respiration, and core temperature) over HTTP. In this prototype the data is synthetic, but the system is designed for real sensors.
  2. Local system: The crew’s onboard system works as a Wi-Fi access point, receives the data, and processes it using I-MR (Individuals and Moving Range) control charts to detect abnormal behavior, and linear regression to identify trends and anticipate anomalies.
  3. Cyclic memory: The local system stores data in a circular buffer, where each new sample replaces the oldest one. This keeps a recent history without overloading the system.
  4. Earth backup: The data is sent to Earth through an HTTP tunnel, where the full history is preserved. This gives doctors a more complete record for precise clinical analysis.

Why it matters: The crew can detect anomalies on their own, without relying on constant communication with Earth, which is critical on long-duration missions. Meanwhile, Earth keeps the complete record for deeper medical analysis.
